questions.question: In the context of Sufi tradition, the term ‘khanqah’ stood for:

questions.question: Bhimbetka, a world heritage site, is known for:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 2 i.e., **__prehistoric rock shelters__**

__
 
• **Bhimbetka, **a world heritage site, in** the Raisen district **of the state of **Madhya Pradesh **is known for its **prehistoric rock shelters.**
 
• It is a** UNESCO World Heritage Site **that consists of seven hills and over 10 km. It was designated so in the year **2003.**
 
• Most of the credit to discover the caves goes to **Shri V.S. Vakankar.**
 
• The Bhimbetka site consists of the following :
 
 
• Paleolithic evidence from excavations with shelters indicating the antiquity of human settlement.
 
• Stone and Iron Age walls and floors within the rock shelters.
 
• 400 painted rock-shelters in five clusters.
 
• Forest areas around the rock paintings.
 
• Most paintings are from the Mesolithic era.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Dr Vishnu Wakankar visited the area with a team of archaeologists and reported several prehistoric rock shelters.
 
• The pre­-historic caves of Bhimbetka was discovered in 1957.
 
• It was first noticed by archaeologist Dr Vishnu Wakankar from the train window on his way to Nagpur.
 
• It was similar to the rocks that he had previously studied in France and Spain.
 
• One of the largest prehistoric complexes.
 
• It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site in India.
 
• Bhimbetka cave covers the prehistoric, Paleolithic, and Mesolithic periods, as well as the historic period.

questions.question: Which of the following turns Blue litmus Red?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Vinegar.__**

__
 
• When you will dip blue litmus paper into vinegar, the color will change from Blue to red. as vinegar is an acid that will change the color of** blue litmus paper to red.**
 
• When you will dip the red litmus paper into vinegar, the **color remains unchanged. **This is because the red litmus paper changes into blue when added to a base.
 
• The main use of litmus is to test whether a solution is **acidic or basic.**
 
• Blue litmus paper turns red under acidic conditions and red litmus paper turns blue under basic or alkaline conditions, with the color change occurring over the** pH range of 4.5-8.3 at 25 degrees Centigrade.​**

questions.question: Which of the following option is also termed as the third-tier of democracy in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Local-self government.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Indian Constitution was amended later with an additional level of governance along with the** Central **and the **State governance** by adding the** Panchayats** and **Municipalities** making it a **three-tier government.**
 
• This was done by the amendment to the Constitution in **1992.**
 
• **The 73rd Amendment of the Constitution** has added a new **part IX **consisting of** 16 Articles **and the** Eleventh Schedule** to the Constitution.
 
• The 73rd Amendment added **Articles 243 to 243O** and added the three-tier system of Panchayats - **Gram Sabha, Panchayat Samiti, and Zila Parishad.**
 
• **The Eleventh Schedule** covers **29 subjects** within the functions of the Panchayat.
 
• **The 74th Constitutional Amendment Act** mandated the setting up and devolution of powers to urban local bodies or city governments as the lowest unit of governance in cities and towns.
 
• The 74th Amendment Act added the **Twelfth Schedule** to the Constitution of India. It consists of **18 matters.**

questions.question: Which of the following is **NOT** a determinant of the patterns of drainage system?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 2 i.e., **__Source of the drainage system__**

 
• The factors controlling or determining the drainage pattern in a region include the **topography, slope, structural control, nature of rocks, tectonic activities, the geological history of that region, climatic conditions of the area, etc.**
 
• The geometric arrangements of the streams in a region are known as a **drainage pattern.**

 

 **Types of drainage patterns found in India**
 
 

 **Types of drainage pattern**
 **Meaning**
 
 

 Antecedent or Inconsequent drainage
 The rivers that existed before the upheaval of the Himalayas and cut their courses southwards by making gorges in the mountains are known as Antecedent rivers. Eg.- Indus, Sutlej, Ganga, etc.
 
 

 Consequent drainage
 The rivers which follow the general direction of the slope are known as consequent rivers. Eg - Godavari, Krishna, Kaveri, etc.
 
 

 Subsequent rivers
 A tributary stream that is eroded along an underlying belt of non-resistant rock after the main drainage pattern is called subsequent rivers. Eg.- Chambal, Sindh, Betwa, etc.
 
 

 Superimposed drainage
 It is formed when a stream with a course originally established on a cover of rock now removed by erosion so that the stream or drainage system is independent of the newly exposed rocks and structures. Eg. - Damodar, Subarnarekha, Banas, etc.
 
 

 Dendric Drainage 
 A pattern of drainage which is branching, ramifying, thereby giving an appearance of a tree. Most of the rivers in the Indo- Gangetic plains are of this type.
 
 

 Trellis Drainage
 It is a rectangular pattern formed where two sets of structural controls occur at right angles.
 
 

 Other drainage types
 Barbed pattern, Rectangular, Radial, Annular, Parallel, Deranged drainages, etc.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is **NOT **correct about myopia?

options.text: The vision may be corrected with the help of concavelens.
It is also knownas near sightedness
In the affected eye, the image of a distant object is formed beyond the retina
The person affected by it cannot see beyond few metres.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__In the affected eye, the image of a distant object is formed beyond the retina__**

 
• **Myopia **is a defect of an eye in which it cannot see distant objects clearly.
 
• A person with Myopia can see nearby objects clearly.
 
• Myopia is caused by due to - **High converging power of the lens, and Eye-ball being too long.**
 
• Due to the high converging power of the lens, the image is formed in **front of the retina **and a person cannot see clearly the distant objects.
 
• Myopia or **short-sightedness** can be corrected by wearing spectacles containing a **concave lens.**
 
• **There are three common defects of vision :**
 
 
• **​**Myopia or short-sightedness
 
• Hypermetropia or long-sightedness
 
• Presbyopia.

questions.question: During British rule in India, ‘gomastha’ was:

options.text: a paid servant to supervise weavers, collect supplies, and examine the quality of cloth
an Indian soldier appointed as the in-charge of a cavalry
a village-level official in the revenue-department
an Indian officialin the intelligence department

questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1 i.e., **__a paid servant to supervise weavers, collect supplies, and examine the quality of cloth__**

 
• **Gomasthas** were the paid servants who were appointed by the East India Company to supervise weavers, collect supplies and examine the quality of clothes.
 
• The word **'gomastha'** means agent in **Persian.**
 
• **The gomasthas** were Indian agents of the British East India Company, who signed bonds with the local weavers and artisans to deliver goods to the Company.
 
• The prices of the goods were fixed by the gomasthas.
 
• They acted arrogantly, marched into villages with sepoys and peons, and punished weavers for delays.
 
• A petition by the weavers of **Santipur factory** in** 1801** contained various complaints regarding the gomasthas and their subordinates.

questions.question: Which of the following institutions is responsible for regulating the formal sources of credit in India?
questions.solution:

• RBI was established via the **RBI Act of 1934**, so it is also known as a statutory body.
 
• The nationalization of RBI took place in **1949 and from January 1, 1949, **RBI started working as a government-owned bank.
 
• The original headquarters of RBI were in** Kolkata, but in 1937**, it was shifted to** Mumbai.**
